newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australis says Q1 loss A$51.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Australis says Q1 loss A$51.1 mln.

text.p: Australis Media Ltd reported on Thursday a net loss of A$51.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 1996.
Australis said earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) was A$18.5 million for the first quarter.

Australis reported a net loss of A$33.00 million in the first quarter of 1995/96. The satellite pay television operator said sales for the 1996/97 quarter were A$26.40 million, up from A$5.85 million a year ago.
Total subscribers were 313,000 at the end of September, of which 98,000 where direct Australis subscribers, 95,000 were franchisee subscribers and 120,000 were Foxtel subscribers.
Australis has a programming arrangement with cable pay-TV group Foxtel, which is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and government-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp.

"...The extent and nature of the competitive environment and the immediate and long-term viability of subscription television services in Australia are uncertain and, accordingly, no assurance can be given as to whether, when or whta extent the company will generate net income," Australis said.
"Until the company establishes a sufficient subscrivber base for its broadcast subscription services, it expects to incur signiifcant net losses," Australis said.
Australis reported a net loss of A$251.69 million in the 1995/96 year, compared with a A$122.05 million net loss in 1994/95. Australis shares closed steady at 16 cents.
